nodes.label: Web SPA shell
nodes.summary: Vue 3 entrypoint: mounts App.vue with Pinia, vue-router, unhead and TanStack Query. App.vue hosts RouterView plus the consent banner and GTM bootstrap.
constraints: TanStack Query defaults pin retry:false and refetchOnWindowFocus:false to match the pre-migration fetch-once-on-mount behavior

nodes.label: Router & guards
nodes.summary: createWebHistory router plus a side-effect-free route table. beforeEach runs auth.init() once, enforces requiresAuth/guest/needsTermsAcceptance; afterEach fires a consented pageview.
constraints: routes.ts must stay side-effect free so scripts/prerender.mts can build a guard-free router without touching window or calling auth.init()

nodes.label: Views, components & layouts
nodes.summary: 53 lazily-imported route views (per-monitor-type list/create/edit/detail sets, dashboard, billing, settings, docs, marketing pages) plus shared components, docs partials and the three layouts.
constraints: Never hardcode hex colors — use design tokens from docs/reference/design.md
Tailwind CSS variables must be written bg-[var(--token)], never bg-[--token] (compiles to invalid CSS in this Tailwind v4 setup)

nodes.label: Stores & query composables
nodes.summary: Pinia auth store (session status/user) and one useQuery composable per resource (cron/uptime/ssl/domain/port/dns monitors, billing, incidents, maintenance, status pages, channels, API keys).
constraints: auth.init() must use plain fetch, never api.get — the 401 interceptor would treat 'not logged in' as a session error and redirect (ADR-003)

nodes.label: API client
nodes.summary: Cookie-credentialed fetch wrapper with an ApiError type and a single-flight 401 -> /auth/refresh -> retry interceptor, plus one typed resource module per REST surface.
constraints: Browser session auth is the access_token httpOnly cookie only — never an Authorization header (ADR-003); every request sends credentials: 'include'

nodes.label: Client libs & content
nodes.summary: Pure logic (monitor form validation, notification channel types, theme, consent, analytics, version) plus the static marketing content set: blog posts with split lazy metadata, FAQ and home copy.
constraints: blog/postsMeta.ts must never be eagerly imported from posts/*.ts — Rollup would bundle the whole post module into the eager chunk (INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT)
GTM only loads after consent is granted

nodes.label: API binary (main)
nodes.summary: Loads config, runs goose migrations, opens the pgx pool (MaxConns pinned to 25), constructs every outbound client, registers the Telegram webhook, starts the worker goroutine, then blocks on the HTTP server.
constraints: dbMaxConns = 25 caps the pool explicitly rather than using pgx's max(4, NumCPU) default — the pool is shared by the worker and all live traffic
The worker runs as an in-process goroutine — no Redis, no job queue, no external broker (ADR-001)

nodes.label: HTTP server & routes
nodes.summary: chi router: www redirect, CORS, security headers, 64 KB body cap, compression, per-route httprate limits, the public status page and badge routes, the SPA catch-all, /api/v1 session routes and the X-API-Key-only /api/v1/public group.
constraints: Status pages live at /status/{slug} on the same domain — no subdomains (ADR-005)
/api/v1/public is a separate route group from the RequireAuth group so cookie auth and X-API-Key can never be conflated (ADR-028)
Every route needs rate-limit coverage, either its own httprate wrapper or an enclosing r.Use

nodes.label: Auth middleware
nodes.summary: Two mutually exclusive authenticators: RequireAuth validates the access_token httpOnly cookie into Claims, RequireAPIKey hashes an X-API-Key header, looks it up and stamps the org onto the context.
constraints: Browser session auth is the access_token httpOnly cookie only, never an Authorization header (ADR-003)
The public API authenticates via X-API-Key, deliberately never Authorization (ADR-028)

nodes.label: HTTP handlers
nodes.summary: Request/response layer: auth & terms, the six monitor types, cron ping receipt, notification channels, status pages (private CRUD and public render/badges), incidents, maintenance windows, billing + Paddle webhook, API keys, settings and suggestions.
constraints: Every tenant-scoped query must filter by org_id — a missing filter is a silent cross-tenant data leak
Paddle is the merchant of record; do not switch payment providers (ADR-026)
ping.go routes cron recovery through worker.DispatchAlert rather than duplicating channel dispatch

nodes.label: Background worker
nodes.summary: In-process goroutine: a 30 s ticker runs overdue-cron, stuck-run, uptime, SSL, domain, port and DNS checks (bounded to 50 concurrent outbound checks); a 24 h ticker prunes old data. Owns DispatchAlert, the shared per-channel fan-out with an org-email fallback.
constraints: Goroutine workers are intentional — no Redis, job queue or external broker (ADR-001)
checkConcurrency = 50 bounds concurrent outbound checks per tick
Nil HTTPClient/TCPDialer is the production default and wires through httpsafe to block SSRF to loopback/private/link-local/metadata targets
A monitor always has somewhere to send an alert — an org-wide email fallback fires when no channel delivered (ADR-023)

nodes.label: Alert channel clients
nodes.summary: One client per delivery channel — Telegram bot API, Resend email, outbound signed webhooks, Slack incoming webhooks, Twilio SMS — over deliver.Do, the shared one-attempt, no-retry send-and-classify helper.
constraints: One attempt, no retry — callers record delivery status from (statusCode, err) without inspecting err's type
Telegram is deliberately outside deliver.Do: it returns HTTP 200 and signals failure via a JSON 'ok' field
Twilio auth uses a scoped API Key SID/secret, never the primary Account Auth Token
Outbound webhook and Slack sends dial through httpsafe (user-supplied URLs)

nodes.label: Plan limits & enforcement
nodes.summary: Pure plan table (monitor/status-page/channel caps, min check interval, SMS credits) plus the enforcement pass that pauses over-limit monitors and channels after a downgrade.
constraints: Plans are Hobby $0 / Solo $9 / Startup $29 / Enterprise $99
Enforcement pauses excess resources on downgrade rather than deleting them

nodes.label: sqlc query layer
nodes.summary: sqlc-generated Queries over a pgx pool — one .sql.go per domain (auth, orgs, monitors, uptime, ssl, domain, port, dns, incidents, maintenance, status pages, notifications, billing, api keys, suggestions) plus shared models.
constraints: sqlc only — no ORM (ADR-004)
Generated code is never hand-edited; regenerate from queries/*.sql (hook-enforced)
Every tenant-scoped query must filter by org_id

nodes.label: Config & shared utilities
nodes.summary: Cross-cutting packages: env config loading, the JSON response helpers, the httpsafe SSRF guard (restricted-IP dial blocking, redirect refusal), the terms-version tracker, and the RDAP registry client used for domain expiry lookups.
constraints: httpsafe.BlockPrivateDial must reject loopback/private/link-local/cloud-metadata addresses on every user-supplied outbound target
httpsafe.RefuseRedirects stops a permitted host redirecting into a restricted one

nodes.label: PostgreSQL
nodes.summary: The single datastore. 36 goose migrations define orgs/users, the six monitor tables with their check/ping/incident history, notification channels, status pages and incidents, maintenance windows, billing state and API keys.
constraints: Migrations run automatically at boot via goose.Up — no separate deploy step
Schema is the sqlc source of truth (sqlc.yaml schema: migrations/)
Old pings/checks/incidents are pruned on the 24 h worker tick (ADR-015)

nodes.label: Paddle (billing)
nodes.summary: Merchant of record. Server side calls api.paddle.com (or sandbox-api) for transactions, subscription updates/cancels and portal sessions; the browser opens the Paddle.js overlay; Paddle posts signed subscription events back to /webhook/paddle.
constraints: Paddle is the MoR and handles global tax — do not switch payment providers (ADR-026, supersedes ADR-018 LemonSqueezy)
PADDLE_ENVIRONMENT selects api.paddle.com vs sandbox-api.paddle.com; unset in production
Webhook signatures are verified before any state change

nodes.label: Alert providers
nodes.summary: The outbound delivery destinations: api.telegram.org, Resend, api.twilio.com, Slack incoming webhooks and customer-owned HTTP webhook endpoints.
constraints: All optional — an unset TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN / RESEND_API_KEY / TWILIO_* just disables that channel
Customer webhook payloads are HMAC-signed with X-Checkmeup-Signature

nodes.label: Monitored targets & registries
nodes.summary: Everything the worker reaches out to on a customer's behalf: HTTP endpoints (uptime, keyword and JSON assertions), TLS handshakes for certificate expiry, TCP ports, DNS records, and rdap.org for domain registration expiry.
constraints: Targets are user-supplied — HTTP and TCP checks dial through httpsafe to block SSRF into loopback/private/link-local/metadata ranges
DNS lookups need no SSRF guard: they resolve but never connect
SSL and domain monitors check once per 24 h; uptime is configurable 1/5/10/30 min; the cron worker ticks every 30 s

nodes.label: Google Tag Manager
nodes.summary: GTM container loaded only after the consent banner records a grant; SPA route changes are pushed to dataLayer explicitly since GTM's own pageview trigger only fires on hard load.
constraints: Never loads without granted consent
Skips silently when VITE_GTM_ID is unset (local dev)

flows.name: Cron ping received
flows.trigger: A customer's cron job GETs /ping/{token} (or /ping/{token}/start) when it runs

steps.action: Matches /ping/{token}, rate-limited 60/min keyed by ping token
ReceivePing resolves the monitor by token and computes the next expected ping
Records the ping, closes any open incident and advances next_ping_at
Persists the ping row and updated monitor status
If the monitor was down, sendCronRecoveryAlert routes through DispatchAlert
Fans the recovery message out to every attached channel, or the org-email fallback
Telegram / Resend / Slack / webhook / Twilio deliver the recovery notice

flows.outcome: The monitor is marked healthy with a fresh next_ping_at; if it had been alerting, one recovery notification goes out per attached channel.

flows.name: Uptime check detects an outage
flows.trigger: The worker's 30 s ticker fires and picks up uptime monitors that are due

steps.action: Starts the worker goroutine at boot with the shared Notifiers bundle
checkUptimeMonitors claims due monitors and runs up to 50 checks concurrently
performHTTPCheck requests the URL through the httpsafe dialer and applies status/keyword/JSON assertions
recordUptimeCheck stores the result and opens an incident once the failure threshold is crossed
Persists the check row, monitor status and incident
alertUptimeIncident builds the down alert and calls DispatchAlert
Sends per channel; an org-wide email fires if nothing delivered
Providers deliver the down alert

flows.outcome: A down incident is open in Postgres and one alert event has gone out across every attached channel, subject to the per-incident alert cap.

flows.name: Sign in and load the dashboard
flows.trigger: A visitor submits the sign-in form at /sign-in

steps.action: SignInView's submit() posts the credentials
api.post('/api/v1/auth/sign-in') with credentials: 'include'
Routes to auth.SignIn behind a 10-per-10-minutes per-IP limit
Verifies the password and sets the access_token httpOnly cookie
Looks up the user and their org
Returns the stored password hash and org membership
auth store records the user; router guards now allow requiresAuth routes
beforeEach redirects to the dashboard (or accept-terms when terms are stale)
RequireAuth validates the cookie on every subsequent dashboard fetch

flows.outcome: The browser holds an httpOnly session cookie, the auth store is authenticated, and the dashboard's monitor queries resolve behind RequireAuth.

flows.name: Upgrade a plan through Paddle
flows.trigger: A signed-in user picks a paid plan in the billing screen

steps.action: BillingView requests a checkout, then opens the Paddle.js overlay
POST /api/v1/billing/checkout with the plan and cycle
Routes to billing.CreateCheckout under a 20-per-hour per-org limit
createPaddleTransaction calls the Paddle API for a transaction id
Paddle runs checkout in the overlay, then posts a signed subscription event to /webhook/paddle
Webhook verifies the signature and writes the new plan, cycle and Paddle ids
Updates the org's plan and billing state
On a downgrade, enforcement pauses monitors and channels above the new caps
Persists plan, subscription ids and any paused resources

flows.outcome: The org's plan reflects the Paddle subscription and plan limits are re-enforced; the billing view polls until the webhook lands.

flows.name: Public status page render

steps.action: Handles /status/{slug} in Go before the SPA catch-all, at 300 req/min per IP
Loads the page, its monitor rows, and active plus paginated resolved incidents
Reads status page config, attached monitors and incident history
Returns page, monitor and incident rows
Renders server-side HTML, or an SVG badge for the badge routes

flows.outcome: A branded status page (or cache-controlled SVG badge) is served from the same domain, with no authentication and no subdomain.
